sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s presentation, comorbidities, prior interventions, and the sequence of events leading to a third transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV). Frames how the evolving symptoms and imaging findings prompted reintervention after treated prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE).
subtopics: Baseline profile: late 70s male with CAD (multiple PCIs), hypertension, COPD, diabetes, AV block with pacemaker, history of GI bleeding
Index TAVI (2014): 27 mm Lotus for severe AS; subsequent deterioration by 2021–2022
First redo (2022): TAV-in-TAV with 23 mm Evolut; early hemodynamic improvement; vascular access complication managed surgically
PVE episode (2022): Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia, severe restenosis; 6-week targeted IV therapy then oral therapy; clinical and imaging resolution
Re-worsening (2024): severe prosthetic valve dysfunction (MG 49 mm Hg, AVA 0.5 cm², mod–severe AR) despite EF recovery
Decision for third TAVI (2024): prohibitive surgical risk, complex prior frames; heart team consensus and patient-centered shared decision-making

sections.section_title: Key Pathophysiology and Procedural Risks Relevant to Triple Transcatheter Valves
sections.description: Explains mechanisms of bioprosthetic valve failure after TAVI, the implications of prior PVE, and the anatomic/physiologic hazards unique to serial valve-in-valve procedures that shape planning and feasibility.
subtopics: Structural valve deterioration (SVD): leaflet fibrosis, calcification, pannus; interaction with prior frame geometry
Impact of prior PVE: leaflet injury, mechanical restriction; criteria for proceeding after infection control (culture negativity, TEE/CT without vegetations or paravalvular complications)
Hemodynamic constraints in serial ViV: reduced effective orifice area, risk of severe prosthesis–patient mismatch (PPM)
Coronary obstruction risk: role of sinus size, coronary height, valve-to-coronary (VTC) distance, and neo-skirt formation with layered frames
Coronary reaccess challenges: commissural misalignment and cumulative mesh burden
Guideline context: surgical preference in active/complicated PVE vs individualized TAVI consideration post-eradication with prohibitive surgical risk

sections.description: Details the multimodality imaging and risk assessment that established infection resolution, quantified stenosis/regurgitation severity, and guided device selection, depth, and coronary protection strategy for TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV.
subtopics: Echocardiography: gradients, AVA by continuity equation, Doppler velocity index; grading intraprosthetic AR; LV remodeling and EF course
MSCT for feasibility: lumen diameter within prior valve (Evolut min 13.7 mm), coronary ostial height, sinus of Valsalva dimensions, VTC, anticipated neo-skirt position
Frame–frame interaction analysis: alignment with prior commissures, impact on orifice and coronary flow
Exclusion of active infection: blood cultures, TEE, MSCT
Risk stratification: EuroSCORE II 27.36%, comorbidity burden, prior frame integration implying complex surgical explant
Decision against routine coronary protection based on CT-derived clearances and planned high implantation

sections.section_title: Third TAVI: Strategy, Device Selection, and Procedural Execution
sections.description: Explains the procedural plan emphasizing coronary preservation, commissural alignment, and orifice optimization; describes intra-procedural steps and rationale for each maneuver in the context of a triple-stented anatomy.
subtopics: Device choice: Acurate neo2 (size S) for supra-annular leaflets, favorable hemodynamics in narrow anatomies, and support for commissural alignment
Access and monitoring: local anesthesia; left radial and left femoral arterial access; rapid ventricular pacing
Predilation strategy: 22/40 mm balloon under pacing to assess expansion and confirm unobstructed coronaries via simultaneous aortography
High implantation aligned to Evolut leaflets: aim to pin prior leaflets to frame, minimize neo-skirt below coronaries, preserve reaccess, and improve EOA
Post-dilation: 20/40 mm balloon to optimize expansion; potential partial expansion of prior Evolut frame improving leaflet motion
Commissural alignment technique: leveraging CT models and fluoroscopic landmarks to reduce future access complexity
Immediate procedural endpoints: correct positioning, preserved coronary flow, no paravalvular or transvalvular regurgitation

sections.description: Presents immediate and longitudinal results per VARC-3, interprets early high gradients and subsequent improvement, and consolidates 1-year clinical and echocardiographic durability after TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV.
subtopics: Immediate post-implant TTE: intact leaflet motion, no AR, but MG 67 mm Hg, AVA 0.9 cm², DVI 0.24 indicating severe PPM
Trajectory of improvement: 1 month MG 27 mm Hg, AVA 1.1 cm²; LV reverse remodeling; sustained gradients at 3.5 months and 1 year (MG ~26–27 mm Hg, AVA 1.1 cm², EF ~65%)
Mechanisms of gradient reduction: optimized commissural alignment, effective post-dilation, partial radial expansion of prior frame improving central flow
Safety: no recurrent endocarditis, regurgitation, or valve-related complications; clinical stability and functional recovery
Assessment framework: VARC-3 performance metrics and absence of access-related or coronary complications

sections.section_title: Clinical Lessons and Lifetime Valve Management
sections.description: Synthesizes practical lessons on planning serial transcatheter interventions, balancing infection history with anatomy and risk, and anticipating future access and options in triple-frame configurations.
subtopics: Individualized heart-team decisions: integrate infection control status, surgical risk, and detailed CT feasibility over guideline defaults
Plan for lifetime management from the first TAVI: anticipate frame layering, commissural alignment, coronary reaccess, and EOA preservation
CT as the cornerstone: measure VTC, sinus dimensions, coronary height, and model neo-skirt relationships to tailor device and depth
Device selection principles in redo ViV: supra-annular hemodynamics, frame height, alignment capability
When to consider adjuncts: high implantation, strategic post-dilation; awareness of limitations of leaflet laceration/BASILICA or bioprosthetic fracture in triple frames
Counseling on future constraints: potential difficulty of coronary interventions and limited options if current prosthesis fails
